Railroad To Heaven - Elko, NV by Sean Christopher Flansbaum
Source: Railroad To Heaven - Elko, NV by Sean Christopher Flansbaum

patrol on the borders of the southern radlands was a dull, but inherently unhealthy posting. rob stomped out the last cigarette in the packet, and slipped on the gas mask that health and safety did their best to force everyone to wear when one was so close to the edge. he looked at the horizon through the clear lens of the mask.

the area looked just fine, plants were growing, nothing was amiss, but he knew that if he followed that land far enough to stand on the hills just out of the horizon, he would see the great bomb craters, and Geiger counters would shriek at you with the intensity of a banshee.

he looked farther down the track, it had been hardly used since the breakage war and the only ones who could be using it were smugglers, or from the Texan states who controlled the other end of the track. but texas's direction was to robs back, and they only stuck to their own country, not stumbling over to this one.

he squinted his eyes as his ears picked up the faintest tracers of sound, of train horns and rumbles. nothing was charging in from the radlands. rob turned around, and the headlight coming toward his back, still very far away, was a firefly beacon. he hopped off the track, still unsure with no orders forwarded for this to happen.

the train swept by with great urgency when it did come. rob saw hundreds of brown camoed texan troops looking at him, he saw the cargo traincars holding military vehicles in packs. he saw that the train was still coming from the horizon. no end was in sight.

We’re very excited to reveal to you what we have in store for Verdun. Our firm dedication to create an all-encompassing World War I experience for the players is taking form in this roadmap.

During our early access process we proved our dedication and ability to update the game, gathering praise for being one of the only early access titles to do so. With over 200 updates in less than 2 years which means an update roughly every 3 days, we gained a reputation of dedication and efficiency. Expect the same kind dedication and professional attitude in the future. In addition we shall continue to communicate with the community with the same passion for good game development as we did vividly in our Early Access phase.

The goal of this roadmap is to refine and polish the experience of the core framework we created at our launch. Our team has set several milestone updates in which we specifically aim to polish several rough elements currently existing in the game. On top of this we want to excite our players with awesome new and unique experiences and bring never seen before world war I content to life. This will happen in several massive, Free Thematic Expansion Packages that will be rolled out every few months. These packages will include Game Modes, Maps, new Squads, weapons and uniforms. We are especially excited for the new nations that will enter the game: The Kingdom of Belgium and The United States of America, both playing a pivotal role in the war on the western front. Note this roadmap may be subject to change and reflects our ideal plan for the future we will remain flexible in how in what order we will add these.

“Flanders Fields” - Free Thematic Expansion Pack

The Flanders Fields DLC will feature the dogged Belgian squads pitted against the rigid German Schutze sentries. They will both wield unique defensive weapons and equipment including trench magazines, heavy mortars and body armour. In addition this update will see a long requested feature and one of the most famous icons of the Verdun and the war: Fort Douaumont. We have taken great care in research and visited the fort to make it true to life. Now it is your turn to capture the fort!

“Horrors of War” - Free Thematic Expansion Pack

With the horrors of war DLC we want to elevate the gritty experience in Verdun to new heights. The first part of this will be a complete overhaul of the in-game gore system. The second part will be a much desired focus on the realism and the introduction of a classic territorial “offensive” game mode with fixed historical scenarios and hardcore gameplay. An exciting night raid map will accompany the experience.

“Squad Veterans” - Free Thematic Expansion Pack

At the very core of Verdun is the squad gameplay. With the base game we only scratched the surface of what is possible with the unique squad co-op system we have created during the early access period. In the ‘Squad Veterans’-DLC players will get new ways to work together in CO-OP to defend their trenches against a much larger force.

“The yanks are coming!” - Free Thematic Expansion Pack

This DLC fulfils the desire of so many fans asking us for one thing: The inclusion of the US into the game. They will be very pleased as the United states will be represented by no less than 2 unique squads, one Army and one Marine. Equipped with a range of unique weaponry the fresh marines will face stiff opposition from flamethrower-wielding German Pioniers. This DLC extends the choices the players have in frontlines squad matches immensely as the total of available squads and ways to play with friends reaches no less than 12. To up that the American experience will be accompanied by a all-trench battle in the champagne region scenario!

Future Expansions?

The war was not limited to the western front. With the closure of this part of the development a new world of opportunities opens up as several other theaters-of-war can be created such as:

The southern front, with unique mountain-warfare scenarios with Italian and Austro-Hungarian troops battling the alpine peaks.

The immeasurable eastern front where Russia, Germany and Austria engaged in massive maneuvers in fast landscapes.

The Balkan front in which many factions were pitted against each other.

The Middle Eastern front, which was the site of several infamous battles including the Ottoman empire such as the beach landings at Gallipoli, Suez Canal and the siege of Kut.

The African Theatre, a must dynamic front with asymmetrical guerilla warfare in horrible jungle conditions.

The when and how of the implementation of these front depends on technology, the market, the community and our own budget. Obviously adding an entire theatre-of-war requires a great amount of time and resources but also the the right place either in addition to the base game, part of a bigger expansion pack or worthy of an entirely new game and graphics altogether. Regardless of the choice; the desire on part of the developers is there!

Kelly Thomas (April 5, 1974 – July 10, 2011) was a homeless man diagnosed with schizophrenia who lived on the streets of Fullerton, California. He was beaten by Jay Cicinelli, Manuel Ramos, and Joseph Wolfe, three members of the Fullerton Police Department, on July 5, 2011. Thomas was taken to St. Jude Medical Center before being transferred to the UC Irvine Medical Center, where he was comatose on arrival and not expected to recover. He never regained consciousness, and died on July 10, 2011.[2][3]

Medical records show that bones in his face were broken and he choked on his own blood.[4] The coroner concluded that compression of the thorax made it impossible for Thomas to breathe normally and deprived his brain of oxygen.[5] His parents removed him from life support five days later, and he died from his injuries on July 10, 2011.[6] Officer Manuel Ramos was charged with one count of second-degree murder and one count of involuntary manslaughter; Corporal Jay Cicinelli and Officer Joseph Wolfe were each charged with one count of felony involuntary manslaughter and one count of excessive force.[5][7][8] All three pleaded not guilty.

A judge declined to dismiss the charges against the officers in January 2013, finding that "a reasonable person could infer that the use of force was excessive and unreasonable."[9] An appeals court judge also denied a request to overturn the lower court's decision.[10] On January 13, 2014, Ramos and Cicinelli were found not guilty of all charges,[11] while the trial for Wolfe was pending.[12] Following the verdict for the two officers, the district attorney's office announced it would not pursue the case against Wolfe.[13]
